"Buzzword for CC that removes control of movement: Airborne, Forced Action, Root, Sleep, Stasis, Stun (Suspension), Suppression..." — the vocabulary the wiki 'Immobilize' tip in the Mandate text resolves to.

No entry: grep for cc_scope / scope / mandate / abyssal / immobilize / crowd control returns nothing relevant (only an unrelated 'role-scoped subset' at line 350 and the coupled-timeline objective f(S) at lines 349-390). The math doc does not constrain this leaf; the determination rests on the cached wiki text.

step_1_identify_which_effect_in_this_sce: The scenario name pins two items: Imperial Mandate (4005) and Abyssal Mask (8020, whose curse aura the name 'abyssal_curse' refers to; the current cached passive name is 'Unmake').

Of the two, only Imperial Mandate carries any crowd-control atom: data/item-atoms/4005.json has crowd-control-mobility.immobilize, and data/atoms/items.json['4005'] has control.immobilize sourced from 'passive:Command@kw:immobilize'.

Abyssal Mask carries no crowd-control atom at all (only stats + damage.magic). A field named cc_scope therefore cannot describe the Abyssal Mask curse event; it must describe the Imperial-Mandate-side immobilize/Vulnerable event.

A scan of every passive/active branch in data/items.json for 'immobiliz' confirms Imperial Mandate is the only immobilize-conditioned item in this scenario's named pair (other hits — Fimbulwinter, Solstice Sleigh, Bandlepipes, Force of Entropy, Cruelty, Reverberation, Black Hole Gauntlet, Turbo Chemtank — are not in this scenario).
step_2_read_the_scope_out_of_the_cached_: Imperial Mandate / Command: 'Immobilizing AN ENEMY CHAMPION marks THEM as Vulnerable for 4 seconds, increasing the damage THEY take from all sources by 7%.'
Grammatical scope: the object of 'marks' is the singular 'an enemy champion' that was immobilized. The mark is attached to that champion, not to a location, not to a radius, not to nearby enemies.

The follow-up sentence confirms per-target bookkeeping: 'Subsequent immobilizes AGAINST A TARGET extend the duration of the effect' — duration state is keyed per target, which only makes sense for a target-scoped debuff.

There is no radius, no 'nearby', no 'enemies around', and no area term anywhere in either Imperial Mandate branch. The full text of both branches was dumped and inspected (they are two strings total).

Contrast control: Abyssal Mask / Unmake DOES carry an explicit area term — 'Enemy champions within 700 units of you become cursed'. The cache therefore demonstrably spells out area scope when an effect has one. Its absence in the Mandate text is meaningful, not an omission.
step_3_conclusion: Correct scope for the Imperial-Mandate Vulnerable application event = per-immobilized-champion, i.e. SingleTarget.

The previous state (<absent>) declared no scope. For an event whose entire semantics are 'this debuff lands on the champion that was immobilized', an undeclared scope is under-specified and is the strictly more dangerous default in a roster/coupled fight: with no scope the 7% Vulnerable amp can be applied like the Abyssal 700-unit aura, i.e. to every enemy in the roster, which the cached text does not support.
SingleTarget matches the cached wiki text; <absent> does not encode the text at all. Verdict: new_value_correct.

scope_and_limits_of_this_determination.what_was_NOT_available: The scenario definition for 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' does not exist anywhere under data/ (grep for the scenario id, for 'cc_scope', and for 'support_events' across the whole export returns zero hits). It lives in the forbidden trees (scripts/ or tests/), so the concrete identity of support_events[2] could not be read directly.
scope_and_limits_of_this_determination.how_the_identification_was_made_instead: By elimination over the effects the scenario name pins: Imperial Mandate is the only crowd-control-bearing effect in the pair (per data/item-atoms/4005.json vs data/item-atoms/8020.json), so it is the only effect a cc_scope field can be describing. Indices 0 and 1 evidently did not gain the field, consistent with them being non-CC support events (the support scanner's known event families in data/champion-audit are heals and shields, with scopes like 'self', 'one_teammate', 'self_and_all_teammates' — see batch-e9-1.json lines 424 and 520).
scope_and_limits_of_this_determination.residual_risk: If support_events[2] were instead an ally champion's own area immobilize (e.g. a knock-up ring or a multi-target root) rather than the Imperial Mandate Vulnerable application, the correct scope would be an area value and SingleTarget would be wrong. That alternative could not be excluded from data/ alone. It is disfavoured because (a) the scenario is named for its two items, not for a champion, and (b) Abyssal Mask contributes no CC, so the field's existence in this scenario is most economically explained by the Mandate mark.
scope_and_limits_of_this_determination.confidence: high on the rule (Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable mark is target-scoped, not area-scoped — this is unambiguous in the cached text); medium-high on the binding of that rule to this specific array index.

asides_flagged_not_part_of_the_verdict.observation: The atomizer triple-parses Imperial Mandate's single '20 ability haste' phrase from the Control branch into three unrelated families in data/atoms/items.json['4005']: stat.haste = 20 flat, timing.cooldown = 20 flat, and control.immobilize = 20 flat. The real quantity is 'immobilizing abilities get CDR equivalent to 20 ability haste' — it is not a flat stat (the item's actual stats.abilityHaste is 15), not a cooldown in seconds, and definitely not an immobilize magnitude.
asides_flagged_not_part_of_the_verdict.impact: If any consumer reads control.immobilize.values[0] as a magnitude, or sums stat.haste with stat.ability_haste, Mandate would be overstated by 20 haste. Worth checking; off-task for this receipt.
